title: Benefit-Harm CATE Correlation in Randomized Binary Endpoint Panels with Shrinking Signal Energy
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier subfield below field floor; math and rubric pass without findings, but projected paper-score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4 and no salvageable repair within scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a matching minimax order characterization for squared risk and finite-honest expected interval length; first-order precision means rate order, without efficient constants or Gaussian inference. The shared-sign likelihood factorization, fixed-sample multinomial integration, deterministic energy separation, and separate energy/angular comparisons discharge the converse rather than leaving its central step assumed. The framing contains no stale matched-frontier overclaim, and the distinction from [Guo et al.'s fixed-law correlation theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.01849v2) and [sparse-linear signal-dependent bounds](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1605.07244) is supported by their public theorem text. The contribution remains confined to known uniform scalar design, fair randomization, known smoothness, and public positive energy shells, so the clinical connection establishes a prospective benchmark rather than an operational analysis of benefit–harm data. No delivered worked asymmetric examples or computations demonstrate when the cross branch binds or when the conservatively calibrated intervals become informative. Those scope and practical-evidence limitations constrain the projected paper score and prevent a flagship assessment. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matching finite all-radius minimax squared-risk and finite-90%-honest expected-length orders for the declared shrinking-energy CATE-correlation benchmark, with total original-record procedures and same-class lower constructions. Independent math and rubric panels passed without findings after a positioning repair, but the cold referee assessed subfield below the fixed field floor (paper-score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4); independent maximality and terminal checks found no scoped field-clearing repair. Formalization was not entered: these are reviewed informal derivations, with no Lean proof or axiom verification; re-anchor at subfield only under a future operator instruction.
tldr: We prove an explicit matching frontier for causal benefit--harm CATE alignment in independent randomized binary endpoint panels: minimax squared risk is comparable to \(\Delta^2\), and minimax expected length of connected intervals honest at finite level \(0.90\) is comparable to \(\Delta\). The evaluated \(\Delta\) combines two first-order terms, two unknown-energy terms, and the minimum of three cross-panel powers, with outer saturation and no logarithmic loss. Total original-record procedures attain these bounds for every positive allowed radius, sample size at least two, and arbitrary endpoint imbalance. Same-class Bernoulli testing priors give the matching converses. Consistency is exactly \(n_kr_k^{2+1/(2\beta_k)}\to\infty\) at each endpoint; the balanced equal-smoothness first-order region has its elbow at \(\beta=1/4\). The result concerns correlation across covariates of conditional treatment effects, not a supplied coupling of individual effects.
gap: Published shrinking-signal sparse correlation theory and fixed-law model-free correlation inference do not, in the inspected results, evaluate the full positive-band H"older frontier with finite honest expected length.
fill: The kernel asks for explicit all-radius risk and interval-length functions, total attaining procedures, and same-class original-record converses, with necessary and sufficient public resource conditions.
